scope: Read-only review of ranking.json review_pool; abstract and official repository/model card where located. These are provisional reading notes, not executed validations or final recommendations.

reviews.title: Image Recognition with Online Lightweight Vision Transformer: A Survey
reviews.claim: Surveys lightweight ViT strategies (component design, dynamic networks, distillation) and compares ImageNet-1K accuracy, parameters and throughput.
reviews.official_code_url: https://github.com/ajxklo/Lightweight-VIT (paper project page; survey/supporting code, not a candidate model implementation)
reviews.license: Unverified; repository license not checked in this pass.
reviews.resource_evidence: Survey; no one model's CPU timings or RAM established. ImageNet-1K comparison is the stated evidence.
reviews.reason: Useful map for vision candidates, but not itself a deployable model. Candidate github_url https://github.com/IBM/CrossViT is a mismatch: paper's own project URL is ajxklo/Lightweight-VIT; don't attribute CrossViT as its code.
reviews.next_test: Use the survey to select a concrete architecture; benchmark only if it improves a current image task baseline on target CPU.

reviews.title: VisionWeave: Weaving Elastic Visual Representations as a Native Capability of MLLMs
reviews.claim: Adaptive visual token granularity reports 43% fewer tokens while retaining 98.9% of base performance; serving throughput +2.3x. Evaluation scales Qwen3.8-27B and reports >30K A100 GPU-hours.
reviews.official_code_url: https://github.com/FFY0/VisionWeave (candidate link; primary paper has no verified official repo link in examined abstract)
reviews.resource_evidence: Training scale explicitly >30,000 A100 GPU-hours; 4B and 27B MLLMs. Clearly not a CPU-small model.
reviews.reason: Relevant as a current vision efficiency paper, but it optimizes large MLLM visual tokens and its resource profile is far outside target. No inference claim should be read as CPU deployment evidence.
reviews.next_test: No local reproduction. Reconsider only if serving a large MLLM and visual token/latency overhead is the measured bottleneck.

reviews.title: Squeez: Task-Conditioned Tool-Output Pruning for Coding Agents
reviews.claim: Fine-tuned Qwen 3.5 2B selects the smallest verbatim evidence block for a focused query; 0.86 recall/0.80 F1 while pruning 92% of input tokens, tested on 11,477 examples including a curated 618 test set.
reviews.resource_evidence: Qwen 3.5 2B LoRA fine-tune; no CPU latency/RAM in reviewed abstract. No evidence it removes the need for stored archive/retrieval; task is selective context input. Official README also offers a smaller extractive ModernBERT alternative; performance parity with 2B is not established.
reviews.reason: Promising concrete token/context pruning for coding agents with curated test set and explicit recall/F1; evaluate against repo's current output-elision pipeline. Not a search-result reranker. The githubRepo identity must match KRLabsOrg, not the unrelated CLI compressor.
reviews.next_test: Offline, held-out replay only: measure retained-evidence recall, task success, token reduction and p95 latency against simple grep/rule truncation and current context handling; no agent actions.

reviews.title: SWE-Pruner: Self-Adaptive Context Pruning for Coding Agents
reviews.claim: Task-aware 0.6B neural skimmer selects relevant code lines; paper reports 23–54% token reduction on agent tasks and up to 14.84x compression on LongCodeQA with minimal impact.
reviews.resource_evidence: 0.6B skimmer; README says reuse/reproduction recommends at least 4 GPUs; HF code-pruner card available. The paper also includes CPU claims only indirectly; do not infer practical CPU speed from model size.
reviews.reason: Directly targets code context rather than generic text compression, with artifacts and reproducibility material. However benefit overlaps existing context compression work; compare with current rule-based elision before adopting.
reviews.next_test: Read-only static integration review, then offline trajectory replay comparing recoverable line selection vs current elision; report task success, tokens, overflow, latency. Avoid expensive training; use published checkpoint if permitted.

reviews.title: DeepCode: Open Agentic Coding
reviews.claim: Autonomous document-to-code reproduction combines blueprint distillation, repository indexing/memory, retrieval and closed-loop error correction; authors claim strong PaperBench results.
reviews.resource_evidence: Agent framework requiring LLM and repo tool loop; no CPU budget or compact model claim. Paper/repo evaluations depend on external models and compute.
reviews.reason: Could reduce paper-to-repo implementation friction, but reported high-stakes comparative claims are author-reported and broad; doesn't directly satisfy local CPU classification/extraction. Inspect architecture before any safe benchmark.
reviews.next_test: Compare a small set of public reproduction tasks with human baseline using no write-capable credentials and score test pass rate, fidelity, tool calls and cost.

reviews.title: EfficientLLM: Efficiency in Large Language Models
reviews.claim: A benchmark evaluates architecture, finetuning, and quantization over 100 model-technique pairs (0.5B–72B); reports int4 up to 3.9x memory/energy reduction with 3–5% accuracy drop and task-dependent trade-offs.
reviews.resource_evidence: Study run on 48 GH200 + 8 H200 GPUs; explicitly production-class cluster. Not a CPU-ready artifact or evidence of practical local model quality.
reviews.reason: Useful background for quantization tradeoffs, but its execution/evidence base is large GPU training/inference and the candidate offers no directly targeted CPU classifier/extractor. Ranking metadata points to DLYuanGod/EfficientLLM, but authorship as official code was not verified; treat repo link as unconfirmed.
reviews.next_test: Use only its published benchmark tables to shortlist quantization; benchmark the target model on actual CPU with task accuracy and peak RSS.

reviews.title: GLiNER multi-task: Generalist Lightweight Model for Various Information Extraction Tasks
reviews.claim: Extends GLiNER encoder approach beyond zero-shot NER to QA, summarization, relation extraction and self-learning; reports strong/SoTA task results in the paper abstract.
reviews.official_code_url: https://github.com/urchade/GLiNER (associated official framework; exact multi-task checkpoint/release needs pinning)
reviews.license: Repo is Apache-2.0; checkpoint license is model/version-specific and must be checked before use.
reviews.resource_evidence: Paper calls it a small encoder, but reviewed abstract supplies no parameter count/CPU timings. Prior GLiNER line has CPU evidence, but do not transfer those measurements automatically to this multitask variant.
reviews.reason: Relevant extraction family, but broad tasks and claims need task-specific validation; overlap with GLiNER2 already in this pool makes a second generic GLiNER reproduction redundant.
reviews.next_test: Only test if an unmet extraction schema is identified; choose a single task and compare exact-span F1, structured validity, CPU latency/RSS with existing GLiNER2 and baseline.

reviews.title: Return of the Encoder: Maximizing Parameter Efficiency for SLMs
reviews.claim: Primary abstract reports 47% lower first-token latency and 4.7x throughput on edge devices; distillation improves up to 6 average performance points. Official README separately reports 330M CPU latency 1591ms; these numbers are author measurements, not this run.
reviews.resource_evidence: Official README reports 330M model CPU latency 1591ms, GPU 86ms, NPU 189ms; 1B-scale artifacts. Training requires torchrun/GPU and teacher checkpoint; CPU infer path provided. Paper says it isolates architecture under matched data/params/optimization.
reviews.reason: Strong primary CPU/latency and matched-architecture evidence; useful for classification/summarization-style text2text if generation is actually required. More compact encoder classifiers likely beat it for fixed-label classification.
reviews.next_test: Compare 330M checkpoint to existing CPU baseline on one local text2text extraction/summarization task, controlling input/output lengths, runtime, threads, quality and peak RSS.

reviews.title: Designing Large Foundation Models for Efficient Training and Inference: A Survey
reviews.claim: Primary title differs from HF metadata. Survey of efficient foundation-model training/inference; official survey repository linked by arXiv.
reviews.resource_evidence: No model artifact or CPU workload; survey only.
reviews.reason: Not the title in ranking.json (that title belongs to a different paper), and not a new reproducible CPU-small model. Do not ground an experiment on the stale/mismatched pool title.
reviews.next_test: If needed, reclassify the candidate by its real title and use it as literature only; no experiment.

reviews.title: Continually Post-training Small Models via Synthetic Self-distillation
reviews.claim: SynthSelf outsources synthetic in-distribution supervision to a minimally larger same-family aligner, combining off-policy supervision and rejection sampling; evaluates 4 acquisition datasets, 14 retention benchmarks and 3 small-model scales versus 6 methods. Primary abstract now retrieved.
reviews.resource_evidence: Unknown; do not infer CPU capability from title or HF metadata.
reviews.reason: Potentially relevant due recency but evidence/readiness insufficient; no official code/model or resource claim confirmed.
reviews.next_test: Inspect official artifacts and training requirements before CPU inference comparisons; measure acquisition gains and retention regression separately.

reviews.title: The Other Half of the Memory Wall: Serving 35B MoEs from SSD with Trained Routing Prediction
reviews.claim: Edge0 trains next-layer routing prediction and serves a 35B MoE at 20 tok/s on a single 24GB machine, 3GiB peak active memory; 8B tier also claimed.
reviews.license: Unknown from primary abstract; verify repo/checkpoint license separately.
reviews.resource_evidence: Primary abstract explicitly requires 19.5GB 4-bit weights for the 35B model and a 24GB machine. 3GiB is peak active memory, not full storage. Exceeds this run 2GB download cap; accelerator type unverified.
reviews.reason: Interesting trending systems work, but it targets large MoE model serving; 3GiB active memory can misleadingly imply whole model fits in RAM.
reviews.next_test: None for current task; only reconsider if a GPU/SSD MoE serving bottleneck is in scope.

reviews.title: Efficient Post-training Quantization with FP8 Formats
reviews.claim: Across 75 architectures, compares E5M2/E4M3/E3M4 FP8 versus INT8; author-reported workload coverage 92.64% versus 65.87%. Includes NLP and computer vision, not only LLMs.
reviews.license: Apache-2.0 repository; deployment/model terms still require verification
reviews.resource_evidence: FP8 generally requires supported accelerators; no evidence in reviewed source that it improves x86 CPU inference. Pool's vision classification match is irrelevant.
reviews.reason: Hardware/runtime dependent quantization study. CPU acceleration for this experiment is unverified; retain B for conditional investigation, not an established CPU speed gain.
reviews.next_test: Only reconsider if target CPU ISA/runtime has native FP8; otherwise use int8/int4 CPU-specific baselines.

reviews.title: GLiNER2: An Efficient Multi-Task Information Extraction System with Schema-Driven Interface
reviews.claim: Unified encoder does NER, classification and hierarchical schema extraction; reports 205M parameters, CPU deployment, and around 2.6x CPU speed vs GPT-4o API in classification; benchmark table also includes smaller specialist baselines.
reviews.resource_evidence: Paper reports 205M parameters and CPU latencies 130–208ms across 5–50 labels, but does not fully specify general CPU hardware in table snippet. CPU baseline times include GPT-4o network/API 358–463ms and DeBERTa 1714–16897ms. Official README says CPU-first/no GPU required. No retraining required for initial schema test.
reviews.reason: Concrete compact schema-driven extraction plus classification, an official Apache-2.0 repo, and CPU measurements. Existing prior GLiNER experiments mean avoid repeating generic NER/benchmark; select a novel schema/task that existing local study has not covered.
reviews.next_test: First inventory past GLiNER/GLiNER2 tests to avoid duplication. If uncovered use-case exists, test one structured schema, exact field/span F1, JSON validity, CPU latency/RSS and compare against existing pipeline; pin model revision/license.

reviews.title: Coding-Agent Benchmarks Should Match Their Users' Task Flows
reviews.claim: From 4,782 IDE sessions, real user task flows cover questions/planning/review/refactor/execution beyond issue-fix benchmarks; sequential SWE-Bench Pro pilot roughly doubles cost without stable resolve-rate change.
reviews.official_code_url: https://github.com/JetBrains-Research/SWE-TaskFlow-Generation-Public (candidate official repo from primary paper/HF page; inspect before use)
reviews.resource_evidence: Benchmark/data analysis; no model/CPU inference claim. Pilot on 700 SWE-Bench Pro issues; cost and resolve rate are paper-reported.
reviews.reason: Useful evaluation design signal for AI-driven development; helps avoid overfitting to issue resolution. Not itself a coding agent or CPU model.
reviews.next_test: Map actual desired workflow (including questions/review) before evaluating agents; create a small held-out trajectory set and measure user-task completion, not only SWE-Bench patch resolution.

reviews.title: LSNet: See Large, Focus Small
reviews.claim: Large-small convolution combines broad perception and local aggregation; lightweight model family reports competitive efficiency across vision tasks.
reviews.official_code_url: https://github.com/THU-MIG/lsnet (official PyTorch code; paper also lists jameslahm/lsnet, likely mirror/author alias, pin canonical project)
reviews.resource_evidence: Official README says throughput tests used NVIDIA RTX3090, so the commonly shown throughput does not establish CPU performance. ImageNet-1K weights available.
reviews.reason: Worth comparing for image classification if existing CNN baseline is insufficient; source's headline speed is GPU-only, not a CPU advantage.
reviews.next_test: Benchmark released small variant on target CPU/runtime against PP-LCNet and current model, identical input shape/threads; report top-1 or domain metric, p95 and RSS.

reviews.title: PP-LCNet: A Lightweight CPU Convolutional Neural Network
reviews.claim: Designed around Intel CPU + MKLDNN; PP-LCNet-0.5x reports 1.9M params and 2.05ms, PP-LCNet-1x 3.0M and 2.46ms on Xeon Gold 6148, batch 1, 10 threads; ImageNet top-1 66.10/74.39 for distilled variants.
reviews.license: Apache-2.0 for PaddleClas repository; verify model weights/data terms before deployment.
reviews.resource_evidence: Paper provides CPU-specific Intel Xeon Gold 6148 + MKLDNN latency and parameter counts. Figures are hardware/software-specific; not a current target CPU measurement.
reviews.reason: Directly relevant CPU image baseline with explicit latency/memory proxy (parameter count) and official code/weights. Ranking github_url https://github.com/ngnquan/PP-LCNet is a third-party PyTorch reproduction and not the official implementation; use PaddleClas.
reviews.next_test: Evaluate PaddleClas official checkpoint vs current image classifier on target CPU, batch 1 and throughput mode; verify preprocessing/class mapping, accuracy, latency, peak RSS, and compare same runtime.

reviews.title: A Survey of Small Language Models
reviews.claim: Survey taxonomy of SLM architectures, compression, pruning, quantization and benchmark datasets/metrics.
reviews.resource_evidence: No model or CPU timing; literature review only.
reviews.reason: Helpful to orient later reading but less actionable than the pool's measured encoder/classifier candidates; no new experiment by itself.
reviews.next_test: Use only to identify a concrete method and primary evaluation; don't reproduce survey claims.

reviews.title: An Empirical Study of Harness Design for Coding Agents
reviews.claim: 176 matched settings across 4 models and SWE-Bench Verified/Terminal-Bench 2.1; rule-based elision before LLM summarization is strongest overall efficiency, making elided text recoverable adds machinery without accuracy gain.
reviews.license: Unknown; no official repo confirmed during read.
reviews.resource_evidence: Study uses 4 models, 176 settings, two coding benchmarks; compute/budget not established in accessible abstract. Findings are directly relevant to context management.
reviews.reason: Evidence suggests start with deterministic elision rather than adding a learned pruner; relevant benchmark/harness methodology and informs whether Squeez/SWE-Pruner duplicates current work.
reviews.next_test: On internal traces, compare rule elision, recoverable elision, summarization and candidate pruners using matched model, task and context budget; track success, overflow, tokens and cost.

reviews.title: GEB-1.3B: Open Lightweight Large Language Model
reviews.claim: Chinese-English 1.3B model trained on 550B tokens; abstract says FP32 has commendable CPU inference speed but provides no quantified speed in reviewed abstract.
reviews.license: Unknown; official code/model URL not confirmed.
reviews.resource_evidence: 1.3B FP32 weights require at least ~5.2GB for weights alone (derived 1.3B×4 bytes; not total RAM); paper abstract gives no measured CPU timing and describes ongoing quantization work.
reviews.reason: CPU claim is vague and model is too large for a small classifier/extractor; no exact resource evidence or official artifact pinned.
reviews.next_test: Only reconsider if the task requires generative bilingual capability; verify checkpoint license and actual CPU speed/RAM before any pilot.

reviews.title: LiteGUI: Lightweight GUI Agents via Multi-Solution Guided Distillation and Dual-Level Reinforcement Learning
reviews.claim: Combines on-policy distillation, retrieval and macro/micro dual-level GRPO; claims state-of-the-art among lightweight GUI models at 2B/3B scale.
reviews.license: Unknown; no official code/model confirmed in reviewed sources.
reviews.resource_evidence: 2B/3B GUI agent models; RL/post-training and vision-language inference likely accelerator-intensive, but exact training/inference budget not available in abstract. Treat GPU need as unknown rather than false.
reviews.reason: Targets GUI interaction, not the requested classification/extraction or software repository coding workflow; broad SOTA claim lacks artifact/resources here.
reviews.next_test: No current experiment. Revisit only if cross-platform GUI automation is a defined use case and official model/code plus resource data are available.
